To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dielectric properties and RF characteristics of porous silicon are very similar to the corresponding values of trap-rich HR Si and quartz, which are commonly used as RF substrates in the frequency range below 40 GHz.

the dielectric properties (dielectric constant and loss tangent) of porous Si in the frequency range of interest (140 to 210 GHz) have values similar to the ones reported in the literature at lower frequencies (i.e., 1 to 40 GHz).
porous silicon can be used as a local substrate for the integration of millimeter- wave devices on silicon wafers, with performance similar to that of other RF substrates.

the development of porous Si-based devices for use as a local RF substrate material for the on-chiperformance of millimeter-wave (mm-wave) devices.
the development of an integrated millimeter-wave circuitry, which is compatible with CMOS technology and which is capable of operating at frequencies up to 200 GHz.
the dielectric properties and the performance of CPW TLines, fabricated on a porous Si layer and operating in the frequency range of 140 to 180 GHz.

the porous Si material is a very attractive substrate for on-chip integration in the mmW range of high-performance millimeter-wave circuits.
porous Si is a promising substrate material for the on-chips integration of millimeter wave devices.
the porous Si substrate is a promising substrate for the fabrication of on-chip integrated millimeter-wave devices.

porous silicon can be used as a substrate for on-chip integration in the frequency range of 140 to 200 GHz.

the dielectric properties and the electrical characteristics of the porous Si CPW TLines were found to be comparable to those of the trap-rich HR Si CPW TLine, which is considered to be the most suitable substrate for the integration of RF/millimeter-wave devices on the Si wafter.

porous Si can be used as a substrate for millimeter-wave devices.
porous Si has a dielectric permittivity value similar to that of the standard CMOS Si wafer, while its loss tangent value is lower than that of the trap-rich HR Si.

porous Si can be used as a substrate for millimeter-wave devices and circuits in the frequency range of interest (140 to 210 GHz), with the performance of the devices and circuits on porous Si comparable to those obtained on trap-rich HR Si, on a standard CMOS Si wafer, and on quartz.
